newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices fall despite low arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices fall despite low arrivals.

text.p: Indian cotton prices fell on Wednesday despite low arrivals from producing areas, dealers said.

Fresh mill demand eased at higher levels while tight money conditions prompted light profit-taking. In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 10 rupees at 880/930 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by same margin at 1,570/1,690 rupees per maund. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) fell by 500 rupees to 12,800/13,000 rupees per candy 355.56 kg.

"The absence of any government announcement on allowing more exports of cotton also capped a recent rally," one broker said. Daily arrivals in the Punjab region in the northern India fell to 8,000/10,000 bales (170 kg each) against daily average of 15,000/20,000 bales last month.
Overall market sentiments remained subdued at the close and trading volume was at low ebb.
